system: You are the White Dragon: a cross-domain systems engineer who transplants proven mechanisms from other fields into AI agent workflows. Be concrete and executable.
prompt:
HOST (unchanged from A3b): three LLM agents (planner -> worker -> checker, all claude-haiku-5-5) apply 14
natural-language change requests to a 30-line configuration state (lines 'service.field = value'; services
['auth', 'billing', 'search', 'cache', 'gateway']; fields ['replicas', 'timeout_ms', 'retries', 'owner', 'region', 'log_level'] plus max_conn and tier that can be added; owners ['alice', 'bruno', 'chen', 'dara', 'emeka', 'farah']; regions ['eu-west', 'us-east', 'ap-south', 'sa-east'];
log levels ['debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error']). Each agent holds its own copy (book). At steps 4, 8, 12 one untouched line of the worker's
working book is corrupted before the worker runs. The planner sees the change request and its book and writes free
prose; the WORKER DOES NOT SEE THE CHANGE REQUEST, only the decoded instruction and its own book (the checker sees
request + instruction + decoded changes). LLM prompts and outputs must stay exactly as they are.

WHAT YOUR LAST DESIGN (A3b, "H-dragon") ACHIEVED, measured on 16 tasks: 932 channel tokens per task (regex proxy;
1,023 BPE o200k), 0.64x the tent baseline (1,468 regex / 1,860 BPE), with full integrity: 48/48 drifts healed at 0
model calls (local repair from the snapshot of the last approved state, verified by a hash), 16/16 copies correct,
0/1,140 truncations accepted (6-digit check value chk6 = sha256 mod 10^6 of the new state, strict decode).
Per edge (regex / BPE tokens per task): instruction 808 / 817; edits 44 / 85 (word ops 'i value', 'xi', 'akk value',
then chk6); door 32 / 32 ('+' approve; '-' + the reject reason coded like an instruction; 0.25 rejects per task,
reasons ~400 characters); forward 49 / 89 (checker -> planner sends chk6; when the planner's codec has not predicted
the approved state from the instruction it replies '?' and the edits are re-sent; 131 of 224 approvals missed);
heal 0. Instruction coding was: fixed templates for frequent sentence shapes, § macros for keys/values found in the
shared book (§kcy = `cache.retries`, §vcy = its value, §Sa = auth, ...), an adaptive dictionary of earlier literals
(D1..D99, rarely re-used), everything else as literal text in « ». 11,405 of 12,934 instruction tokens (88%) were
literal prose. The planner writes ~4,500 characters of prose per task (14 instructions, ~320 characters each), and
rarely repeats a sentence verbatim, but it re-states keys and current/final values from the book constantly and
re-uses a small set of phrasings ("Leave every other key unchanged", "Change no other keys", "currently", ...).

The owner's target is <= 0.2 x the tent = 294 regex tokens per task (and <= 372 BPE) with the same integrity. The
non-prose places already cost ~124 tokens per task; the prose is the floor to break.

METRIC: channel tokens = regex matches of \w+|[^\w\s] over every message (primary). Guard, binding: the same
messages are counted in BPE tokens (tiktoken o200k_base) and a pass on regex counts only if it also holds in BPE (so a
dense base62/hex blob gains nothing). MEASURED FACT about the metric: o200k_base has 47,424 tokens of the form
' ' + two or more lowercase ASCII letters; any space-separated sequence of such words costs exactly 1 regex token and
1 BPE token per word (measured on 2,000 random ones: 2,000 regex, 2,000 BPE).

TWO NEW ARMS TO DESIGN (A3c):
1. H-PRED: a DETERMINISTIC, NON-NEURAL shared predictor for the prose (instruction and reject reasons), identical on
   both sides, e.g. a context model / dictionary built from the shared book, the fixed tables and the task's own
   history. 0 model calls.
2. H-LOCAL (a separate, labelled claim): the same coding with a small local open language model as the shared
   predictor (identical weights on both sides, deterministic inference). Its forward passes are counted as local
   model calls. Compute: 4 CPU cores, 15 GB RAM, no GPU; python with numpy, torch (CPU) and transformers; model
   weights can be downloaded from the Hugging Face hub; the whole live run (16 tasks, ~230 instructions, each
   encoded and decoded) should finish in about 2 hours.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
1. Lossless: the worker reconstructs the planner's instruction byte-exactly; the worker reconstructs the checker's
   reject reason byte-exactly; the state after edits exactly. Asserted on every message.
2. No extra hosted LLM calls; LLM prompts unchanged. The integrity layer of A3b (snapshot repair, chk6, strict
   edits decode, truncation detection on worker -> checker) stays, unless you replace it with something at least as
   strong; you may also redesign edits, door and forward.
3. Out of band, fixed before the run: the initial books, the A3b tables, and any table or PRIMING CORPUS you define.
   A priming corpus may contain planner and checker prose ONLY from seeds 500-531 (disjoint from the test seeds),
   generated before the run with the same agents and prompts (full A3b H-dragon task runs on those seeds are
   available, ~43 Haiku calls each; up to 32 runs). Its one-time size is reported, not counted per task. The codec
   may use any history both sides have already seen in the task (earlier messages, books, snapshots).
4. Floating point: encoder and decoder run on the same machine; you must say how you make the predictor's
   probabilities bit-identical on both sides (and what happens if they are not).

CROSS-DOMAIN LIBRARY (use any, or others you know): holography (every fragment holds the whole; reconstruction by a reference beam); DNA coding, replication proofreading and mismatch repair; error-correcting and error-detecting codes; information theory and source coding (entropy, dictionary and context coding); predictive coding (send only the surprise against a shared predictor); rocketry telemetry and mission control (frame sync, minor/major frames); double-entry bookkeeping and audit; military brevity codes and mission command; music notation (a score is a compressed performance); immunology (self/non-self markers); control theory and cybernetics; linguistics (anaphora, ellipsis, given/new); also arithmetic / range coding, PPM and
context mixing, LZ77/LZ78 and preset dictionaries (zstd, Brotli), grammar-based compression, CTW, speech codecs
(analysis by synthesis), video codecs (motion compensation: predict from the reference frame).

TASK: design both arms. For each: landings (place, depth, order, domain, mechanism); the predictor exactly (model
order, contexts, how the shared book and history enter, escape/backoff, how probabilities are quantised, how the
priming corpus is built if you use one); the coder (arithmetic/range coder precision, termination, length
signalling); how the coded bits become channel text (alphabet, packing) and its cost in regex and BPE tokens; the
exact wire format per edge (instruction, edits, door approve, door reject, forward, heal) as a grammar a programmer
can implement without guessing; for H-local which model (exact Hugging Face id), what context it is given, top-k or
full-vocabulary distribution, quantisation and determinism. Then predict, for each arm, channel tokens per task
(regex and BPE, total and per edge), bits per character of the coded prose, and the integrity. Be honest: if the
target cannot be met, say by how much and predict the true number.

H-pred build rule: start from an empty model (all PPM counts 0; rank tables all 1; char model all 1). Replay the runs in seed order 500 to 531 and steps in order. Reset the task-history buffers at each run boundary but keep the counts. Code each instruction, then each reason (in R mode), then the approved edits through the live model in update mode, exactly as the live codec would, with that step's snapshot. At the end, halve every count once (this ages the counts so they adapt faster) and freeze. Serialise the frozen state (about 1.5 MB). Because it can be rebuilt deterministically from the corpus, the corpus bytes are what is reported.

Live: each task starts from the frozen state and adapts within the task. Both sides update after each message is decoded. The state is discarded at the end of the task.

H-local preamble rule: pick exemplars greedily from the 448 instructions. At each step take the instruction that adds the most distinct word trigrams not yet covered; break ties by lower (seed, step). Stop when adding the next one would push the preamble past 1,400 Qwen tokens; expect about 14 exemplars. Then add the 2 shortest priming reject reasons. Arrange in (seed, step) order, using the block formats given in h_local_predictor.

LEXER. Apply in this order at each position; all entity patterns require (?<![\w-]) on the left. Concatenating the unit surfaces reproduces the text exactly.
- KEY = (auth|billing|search|cache|gateway)\.(replicas|timeout_ms|retries|owner|region|log_level|max_conn|tier)(?![\w-])
- SVC = (auth|billing|search|cache|gateway)(?![\w-])
- VAL = (alice|bruno|chen|dara|emeka|farah|eu-west|us-east|ap-south|sa-east|debug|info|warn|error)(?![\w-])
- FLD = (replicas|timeout_ms|retries|owner|region|log_level|max_conn|tier)(?!\w)
- NUM = \d+
- WORD = [^\W\d]\w*
- WS = \s+
- PUN = [^\w\s] (one character, Unicode included, e.g. →)
- END closes the message.

SKELETON. Each unit maps to a context symbol: KEY, SVC, VAL, FLD and NUM map to the tags ⟨K⟩ ⟨S⟩ ⟨V⟩ ⟨F⟩ ⟨N⟩. WORD, WS and PUN map to their literal string. Each message starts with the virtual context ⟨I⟩ (instruction) or ⟨R⟩ (reason).

Skeleton model: PPM over these symbols with orders 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, then order -1.
- PPMD escape: a symbol with count c has frequency 2c-1; the escape has frequency equal to the number of distinct symbols in the context.
- Full exclusion of symbols already seen at higher orders.
- Update exclusion: update only the orders from the coding order upward.
- When a context's total exceeds 2^13, halve its counts (rounding up).
- Order -1 is a uniform choice over the known skeleton vocabulary not yet excluded, plus NOVEL.
- NOVEL: one class symbol {word, ws, pun} at uniform frequency, then:
  - word: spelled with an order-2 adaptive character model over [A-Za-z0-9_] plus a stop symbol;
  - ws: spelled over {' ', '\n', '\t', '\r'} plus stop;
  - pun: one symbol uniform over 0x110000 code points.
  A novel word joins the vocabulary.

ENTITY SUBMODELS. When the skeleton emits a tag, the identity is coded as a rank r in a candidate list. Lists are built deterministically and deduplicated with the first occurrence kept. Each table is adaptive, counts start at 1, and one escape slot sits at the end. Notation: U = the instruction's units so far, S = snapshot (ordered lines), H = task history, lastK = the last KEY in U, lastS = the last SVC in U or the service of lastK. ListCtx = the previous non-WS unit is one of , ; ( - or the word and/or.

⟨K⟩ candidates, in this order (40 keys at most):
1. if ListCtx: the next key in S after lastK with the same service that is not in U; then the key with lastK's field in the next service of S;
2. keys in U, most recent first;
3. keys in S of service lastS, in book order;
4. keys changed in the last 3 approved steps, most recent first;
5. all keys in S, in order;
6. the remaining keys of the 40-key universe, in service-major order.
Table context: (ListCtx, whether any KEY is in U yet).

⟨S⟩ candidates:
1. the next service in S order after the last SVC in U that is not yet in U;
2. the service of lastK;
3. SVCs in U, most recent first;
4. all 5 services.
Table context: ListCtx.

⟨F⟩ candidates:
1. the next field of lastK's service not yet in U;
2. fields in U;
3. all 8 fields.

⟨V⟩ and ⟨N⟩ candidates:
1. S[lastK], if its type fits (owner, region and log_level take VAL; the others take NUM);
2. same-class values in U, most recent first;
3. NUM only: for the last two NUMs a and b in U: a+b, a-b, b-a, a*b, a//b, 2a, a//2, min(a+b, 9);
4. values of lastK's field in the other services of S;
5. values in the last 20 history instructions, most recent first;
6. VAL only: the domain list of the field, then all 14 values.
NUM escape: digit count 1 to 7 (adaptive), then the digits with an order-1 digit model; this also covers leading zeros.
Table context: (class, previous non-WS skeleton symbol, bucketed as '=', 'to', 'from', '`', '(', 'of', other).

R MODE. Candidate lists put the instruction's keys and values and the decoded edits ahead of H.

LENGTH. END is an ordinary skeleton symbol, so there is no separate length field.

DETERMINISM. Everything is integer counts held in Python dicts and is updated in a canonical order. Both sides update after a message is decoded, and the encoder applies the same update after it has encoded.","h_local_predictor":"MODEL. Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B (base, not instruct). Weights pinned to the snapshot revision hash recorded at download. Loaded as fp32 with attn_implementation='eager', eval mode, under torch.inference_mode.

CONTEXT. Token ids are built at the id level, never by re-tokenising concatenated strings.
- PRE (fixed, about 1,400 tokens):
  - header: 'Instructions written by a planner for a worker who edits a configuration state.\n\n'
  - then, for each exemplar: 'Instruction:\n' + tok(text) + [EOT=151643] + tok('\n\n')
  - then the 2 reasons as 'Reviewer rejection:\n' + tok(text) + [EOT] + '\n\n'
- DYN (per message):
  - the last ≤6 instructions of this task, as Instruction blocks;

landings.place: Channel alphabet: every coded message on every edge
landings.depth: Deep. Replaces the A3b text tokens: any coded payload becomes a mixed-radix numeral whose digits are whole lowercase words.
landings.domain: Information theory (radix and numeral systems) and DNA codons (a fixed alphabet of symbols that each cost the same)
landings.source_mechanism: Over a channel where every symbol costs the same, the best code uses the largest alphabet of equal-cost symbols, and each symbol then carries log2|alphabet| bits.
landings.mechanism: Two frozen word lists. A1 holds the 47,424 lowercase words w (2 or more letters) for which ' '+w is one o200k_base token. A0 is the subset of A1 where w on its own is also one token, so the first word of a message, which has no leading space, still costs 1 BPE token (|A0| is about 2^15 and is frozen offline). The o200k pre-tokenizer splits ' ?[letters]+' into its own chunk, so the cost does not depend on neighbouring words: 1 regex token and 1 BPE token per word, about 15.53 bits per word (the first word about 14.9 bits).

landings.depth: Deep. Exact arithmetic coding that writes directly in base-B digits.
landings.source_mechanism: Arithmetic coding with an unlimited-precision interval, ended by the shortest codeword that lies inside the final interval.
landings.mechanism: Exact rational interval held in Python big ints: (L, W, D) becomes (L*T + W*cum, W*f, D*T). There is no renormalisation and no precision limit, and messages under 1,000 bits make this cheap. Termination: choose the smallest k for which an integer V exists with L/D <= V/(B0*B1^(k-1)) < (L+W)/D. The decoder takes x = V/(B0*B1^(k-1)) and decodes until the in-model END symbol, then reads any trailing check symbols. Waste is less than 1 word per message, about 0.5 on average.

design.priming_corpus:
Used by both arms. Source: the full A3b H-dragon runs on seeds 500-531, all 32 runs, made before the live run with the same agents and prompts. From each run, record in step order every planner instruction (14 per run, 448 in total, about 143 KB) and every checker reject reason (about 8, about 3 KB), each with the snapshot book current at that step and the approved edits. Nothing from the test seeds is included.

H-pred build rule: start from an empty model (all PPM counts 0; rank tables all 1; char model all 1). Replay the runs in seed order 500 to 531 and steps in order. Reset the task-history buffers at each run boundary but keep the counts. Code each instruction, then each reason (in R mode), then the approved edits through the live model in update mode, exactly as the live codec would, with that step's snapshot. At the end, halve every count once (this ages the counts so they adapt faster) and freeze. Serialise the frozen state (about 1.5 MB). Because it can be rebuilt deterministically from the corpus, the corpus bytes are what is reported.

Live: each task starts from the frozen state and adapts within the task. Both sides update after each message is decoded. The state is discarded at the end of the task.

H-local preamble rule: pick exemplars greedily from the 448 instructions. At each step take the instruction that adds the most distinct word trigrams not yet covered; break ties by lower (seed, step). Stop when adding the next one would push the preamble past 1,400 Qwen tokens; expect about 14 exemplars. Then add the 2 shortest priming reject reasons. Arrange in (seed, step) order, using the block formats given in h_local_predictor.

Reported one-time sizes: H-pred = corpus 146.6 KB + word alphabets about 330 KB, about 0.48 MB. H-local = the same plus 988 MB of Qwen2.5-0.5B safetensors.

Truncation (word dropped, word cut, or a cut that leaves a non-word) fails the alphabet, canonical or chk6 check: false accept ≤ 1e-6 per event, as in A3b. '?' means the instruction decode failed (NAK).
edges.example: Step 0: NOPS=1 (0.1 bit) + RANK 0 = set(cache.retries, 5) (0.3 bit) + chk6 391591 (19.93 bits) = 20.3 bits, sent as 2 words, e.g. 'velvet quorum'. Step 5: RANK 0 = del(gateway.log_level), 2 words. A3b needed 3/6 and 2/5.

edges.decode_and_checks: The worker commits S' as the new snapshot and refreshes its hash.

edges.grammar: msg := CODE (at least 1 word; anything that is not '+' is a reject). Stream: the reason in R mode, END (and for H-local: MODE … EOT CHK8 with chk8 = sha256(reason || S) mod 256).
edges.encode: Code the checker's reason with the instruction codec in R mode. The context adds the instruction and the decoded edits, and the candidate lists draw on them first.
edges.decode_and_checks: Strict decode, canonical check, chk8 (H-local); byte-exact assert. The worker reruns with the reason, as in A3b, and its next edits message replaces the previous one.
edges.example: A reason of about 400 chars: H-pred about 1.1 bpc, 29 words; H-local about 0.55 bpc, 15 words.

edges.grammar: msg := CODE (the worker's approved edits message, copied word for word) | '?' (relayed NAK)
edges.encode: Once approved, the checker copies the worker's edits words unchanged. No '?' round trip.
edges.decode_and_checks: The planner decodes with its own instruction and its book (which equals the snapshot), applies the ops, and verifies chk6 against the result. On failure the planner falls back to the checker's copy, as in A3b; expected 0 times. '?' means re-send the instruction in H-pred mode.
edges.example: Step 0: 'velvet quorum' (2 regex / 2 BPE). A3b needed 1+1+3 regex / 2+1+6 BPE.

edges.encode: Before the worker runs: if hash(working book) ≠ snapshot hash, restore the book from the snapshot.
edges.decode_and_checks: The hash must equal the hash of the last approved state. 0 model calls.

design.target_assessment:
The target is 294 regex and 372 BPE tokens per task. Regex and BPE counts are equal by construction here, so the regex limit is the one that binds.

Fixed (non-prose) cost per task, both arms:
- edits: 14.25 messages × about 2.03 words = 29
- forward: 14 × 2.03 = 28; this is the price of keeping chk6 on both edges
- approvals: 14
- total: about 71, plus the reject reasons.

H-PRED (prediction):
- Instruction prose at 0.66 bpc: about 211 bits per instruction, about 14.1 words. 198 tokens per task.
- Reasons at about 1.1 bpc: 0.25 × 29 = 7 tokens per task.
- Total about 276 regex and 276 BPE: 0.188× tent regex, 0.148× tent BPE.
- Break-even: instruction bpc ≤ 0.72. Above that, H-pred misses: at 0.80 bpc it comes to about 307 (0.21×).
- Confidence of meeting the target: about 55-60%. 80% interval: 245-320.

H-LOCAL (prediction):
- About 0.40 bpc, plus 8 check bits: about 9.3 words per instruction. 130 tokens per task.
- Total about 205: 0.14× regex, 0.11× BPE.
- Break-even: about 0.70 bpc. Confidence of meeting: about 85%.
- Its 57k forward passes are reported as local model calls, separate from the zero hosted calls.

Integrity, both arms (prediction): 48/48 drifts healed at 0 calls, 16/16 copies correct, truncations all rejected (false accept ≤ 1e-6 each).

Gate before the live run: build each model on 31 priming runs and measure on the held-out one, all 32 ways. If H-pred's held-out bpc is above 0.72, the honest prediction is H-pred at 71 + 14 × (bits/15.53 + 0.5) + 7. Report that number instead of claiming the target.

Option for the owner: weaken only the forward check to chk10, so it fits in 1 word. That saves about 14 tokens per task (H-pred about 262), but it is weaker than A3b's chk6 on forward, so it is not the default.
design.risks:
1. The bpc figures are estimates, not measurements. A non-neural PPM trained on only 448 instructions may land at 0.75-0.9 bpc, above H-pred's break-even of 0.72; the held-out gate measures this.
2. Haiku's style may drift between the priming seeds and the test seeds. Mitigation: counts adapt within the task.
3. Floating-point nondeterminism in H-local, from MKL or oneDNN choosing different kernels. Mitigated by: identical incremental code paths, MKL_CBWR, the fresh-process proofread decode, chk8 (detects 255/256), and the '?' fallback to H-pred.
4. Qwen tokenisation might not round-trip some Unicode (→) or whitespace byte-exactly. This is asserted at encode time, and such messages fall back to H-pred.
5. Run time: 3 passes × 230 messages at about 18 s each is about 70 minutes. If the machine is slower, drop the proofread pass. That saves about 33% of the time, and chk8 remains as the guard.
6. A0 may hold fewer than 2^15 words. This costs at most a fraction of a bit per message.
7. If the harness strips or alters spaces between words, decoding fails. The canonical check catches this, but such messages would be lost; whitespace must be preserved exactly.
8. Instructions with several ops, or ops the parser does not predict, can make edits 3 words.
9. Reject reasons are under-primed (only about 8 in the corpus).
10. The forward check costs 14 tokens per task to stay as strong as A3b; relaxing it to chk10 would save them, at the cost of a weaker check.
